chunks: And it was narrated from al-Kāhilī, who said:

A man asked him while I was present about a garment dyed with safflower, then washed: “May I wear it while I am in the state of Ihram?” He said: “Yes. Safflower is not from fragrance, but I dislike that you wear what makes people point you out.”

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: a garment or piece of clothing being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.الطِّيبِ: fragrance or perfume, which has legal implications in Ihram
key_terms.الْعُصْفُرِ: safflower dye, mentioned here as not being a fragrance
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of Ihram for hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.يَشْهَرُكَ: makes you conspicuous or causes you to stand out

ai.seo_question: Can a person in the state of Ihram wear a garment dyed with safflower?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a washed garment dyed with safflower may be worn in the state of Ihram, because safflower is not treated as a fragrance. It also adds an ethical consideration: one should avoid wearing clothing that makes one conspicuous among people.
